newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: More Argentines willing to pay bribes - poll.
newsitem.headline: More Argentines willing to pay bribes - poll.

text.p: The number of Argentines who say they are prepared to bribe the police or dodge taxes has risen substantially over the past four years, a poll published on Friday said.

The survey by private pollsters Gallup published in the Clarin newspaper showed almost all Argentines believe their country is riddled with corruption and they are increasingly prepared to bend the rules themselves.

The proportion of those surveyed who said they would bribe a police officer to avoid a fine was 26 percent, up from 23 percent in 1992. Fifty percent said they would accept part of their salary in cash to dodge taxes, up from 35 percent four years ago.

There has been a rash of high-profile corruption cases in Argentina in recent months with public officials accused of graft or manipulating judges. The former head of the customs service was jailed briefly in December.
The Gallup poll of 1,032 people was carried out in the last quarter of 1996 in major centres of population. Gallup estimated it was 95 percent reliable.
